```r
w1 = is.na(d$bedrooms)
w2 = is.na(d$bathrooms)
table(isNABedrooms = w1, isNABathrooms = w2)
```
(Note how I use names for the arguments which appear in the results to describe the rows and the
columns. This helps make the results clearer.)

+ When we have NA for bedrooms, we also have NA for bathrooms
+ When we have actual values for bedrooms, 624 bathrooms values are non-NA but 87 are NA.


Let's look at the 87
```{r}
d[!w1 & w2, ]
```

Let's look at the year of the date sold
```{r}
d$date[!w1 & w2]
```

We actually want the year, not the specific date:
```{r}
table( format( d$date[!w1 & w2], "%Y"))
```

All 2026!

Was the number of bathrooms in the data for these and erroneously dropped or converted to NA when
reading the data, or was it not present?


Let's also understand the NAs for all 3 years:
```{r}
table(format(d$date, "%Y"))
table(isNABedrooms = w1, yearSold = format(d$date, "%Y"))
table(isNABathrooms = w2, yearSold = format(d$date, "%Y"))
```
